stemMd: A solution initially contains 18 g of solute in 120 g of solution. Pure solvent is added until the solute is 12% of the total mass. How much solvent was added?
explanationMd: The solute mass stays 18 g. If the final total mass is m, then 18/m = 0.12, so m = 150 g. Subtract the initial 120 g to get 30 g of added solvent. Check: 18/150 = 12%.

distractorRationale.e: This does not reduce the mass fraction to 12%.
distractorRationale.c: This takes a percentage of the initial mass without solving for the final mass.
distractorRationale.b: This confuses the three-percentage-point change with a proportional mass change.
distractorRationale.d: This is the final total mass, not the mass added.
